newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit caught in range as activity slows down.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit caught in range as activity slows down.

text.p: The ringgit was caught in a narrow groove as speculators played the range in an equally matched demand and supply market, dealers said on Friday.
"It (dollar/ringgit) is caught between the devil and deep blue sea," said a dealer with a U.S. bank in London.
"Everybody wants to buy dollar at 2.5180/85 and sell at 2.5205/10," he said.
He said activity had slowed down considerably, with U.S. funds the main players in the dollar/ringgit market.
Dealers said the ringgit would remained confined to the 2.5180 and 2.5210 range until Monday.
They said the ringgit would move out of its current range only if dollar/majors strengthen substantially.
"There is really mixed interest in dollar/Malay. The crosses against Sing are also stuck in a range," one dealer said.
Earlier, the ringgit recouped overnight losses and returned to its previous range below 2.52 on buying aimed at the Malaysian stock market, dealers said.
At 1125 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5190/97 a dollar against 2.5207/14 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Thursday. The Singapore dollar was at 0.5559/63 a dollar against 0.5557/67.
